text: I will model the fluid directly in metres as the 12 mm annular gap between the two discs, then subtract 36 equally spaced 8 mm-wide radial vane solids. This produces 36 disconnected but jointly meshed passage volumes. I will use conformal tetrahedra from Gmsh, which handles the repeated curved passages without approximating them as rectangular ducts. The five patches will be `friction_face_lower`, `friction_face_upper`, `vanes`, `inner_inlet`, and `outer_outlet`; the first two are kept separate as requested. First I’m checking the installed CAD/export interfaces before constructing the coarse model.

The vane width is interpreted as a constant 8 mm tangential width (straight radial plates), not an 8 mm angular arc. I will extend each subtraction tool 0.5 mm beyond both cylindrical limits solely to make the Boolean robust; the resulting wetted vane faces still run exactly from 95 to 160 mm radius. Now I’m building and rendering the coarse CAD fluid volume, while checking passage count and volume against an independent analytical area calculation.

The preview confirms 36 open radial passages with no unintended bridges. The slight 0.05 mm reduction in the reported global XY extent is expected: vane-centered passage openings do not include the four exact axis extrema, while their cylindrical faces remain at the specified radii. I’m now identifying patches from face geometry (plane orientation or cylinder radius), rather than from bounding-box position, and measuring their areas and radii before export.

Each passage has exactly six faces: two friction planes, two vane sidewalls, one inner cylindrical inlet, and one outer cylindrical outlet. I’m checking the installed face-radius access and then will form explicit face lists with cardinalities 36/36/72/36/36.

The installed kernel exposes the exact cylindrical radius, so inlet/outlet classification is unambiguous. I will now export the five named patch STLs in one conformal tessellation call. Before doing so, I measure the inner/outer radii from the actual final faces, the axial gap from the two friction surfaces, and the vane width as the separation of the two opposing planes of the 0° vane.

The patch export is watertight and conformal: 1,008 triangles, zero open, flipped, or non-manifold edges. For volume meshing I will import the exact STEP into Gmsh and preserve the same five groups by differential geometry: plane normals distinguish friction faces from vane walls, and cylindrical curvature distinguishes the 95 mm inlet from the 160 mm outlet. This avoids any bounding-box patch assignment. First I’m inspecting the imported topology and Gmsh’s surface-type reporting.

The imported topology matches the CAD exactly: 36 volumes and 216 boundary surfaces. I’ll use a deliberately coarse 3.5 mm target tetrahedral size (about three to four elements through the 12 mm gap), write MSH 2.2 for robust OpenFOAM conversion, and retain all 36 volumes in one `fluid` cell zone. This is a first usable mesh rather than a production refinement.

The coarse mesh contains 17,649 points and 56,585 tetrahedra, with Gmsh reporting no ill-shaped tetrahedra after optimization. I’m converting it to OpenFOAM now and will inspect the resulting patch table before running the binding mesh check.

Conversion stopped only because OpenFOAM utilities require a minimal `system/controlDict` even for preprocessing; no mesh files were produced. I’ll add a utility-only control dictionary (no solver or boundary conditions) and a minimal `fvSchemes`/`fvSolution` only to make the case structurally valid for mesh utilities.
With the utility dictionaries present, I’m rerunning only the format conversion and reading back the generated boundary file to verify that all five CAD patch names survived.

All five names survived conversion, with 29,378 initially undefined tetrahedral faces subsequently paired as internal faces; the final boundary contains only the intended five patches. I’m running bare `checkMesh` now, which is the acceptance criterion, and will inspect topology, disconnected-region count, openness, and quality.

The binding `checkMesh` passes. It confirms 56,585 valid tetrahedra, 36 disconnected regions (exactly the 36 vane-separated passages), total volume \(4.00171\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m^3}\), near-zero boundary openness, maximum aspect ratio 8.17, maximum non-orthogonality 67.8°, and maximum skewness 0.807. No advisory exception is expected: the exported STL union is closed and consistently wound, and the volume mesh covers the same CAD fluid boundary.

The advisory `coverage` check warned only to report the patch accounting: all 1,008 triangles are covered, every CAD face belongs to exactly one of the five requested patches, and there are no unassigned or duplicate faces. I am therefore waiving that informational warning as correct coverage, not as a geometry defect.
